title: DNS: distribute authority and manage stale information
focus: Scalability changes who owns data, how long others may reuse it, and what temporary disagreement means.

sources.title: RFC 1034, Domain Names — Concepts and Facilities
sources.limitations: The historical document has many later updates. Its design rationale is used here; it is not a complete current DNS deployment or security specification.

facts.statement: The design goals call for distributed maintenance and caching rather than collecting a continuously consistent copy of the entire database.
The document places the trade among acquisition cost, update speed, and cache accuracy under control of the data source.

retrospective.boundary: Authoritative data owners, delegated zones, resolvers, caches, clients, and update operations form the naming system.
interfaces: Authority → cache: reuse reduces load while retaining information that may become stale.
Delegation → organization: a naming boundary is also an administrative responsibility boundary.

decision.question: How should a team choose freshness behavior for a distributed lookup service?
options: Demand instant global consistency without considering cost or failures.
Choose an explicit reuse window and update plan consistent with the consumer’s tolerance for stale data.
decision.recommendation: State authority, freshness, temporary-failure behavior, and rollback together.
decision.uncertainty: The acceptable window depends on the decision being supported; a historical design principle supplies no universal duration.

rows: Identify the authoritative owner and delegated scope
State allowable age and conditions invalidating cached data
Consumer tolerance and measured update path
Distinguish unavailable answer from absent entity

questions: Why is cached information useful even when it is not current everywhere?
Which organizational failure can defeat a technically valid delegation?
Explain a stale answer without incorrectly calling it fabricated data.
answer_signals: Makes consistency, availability, and operating cost explicit.
Connects technical delegation to ownership and handover.
retrospective.transfer_exercise: Synthetic: a fleet stores remote configuration locally during disconnection. Define who owns it, when it expires, and what operations remain allowed.
retrospective.limits: No live DNS changes or experiments were performed; security requirements for a present-day deployment require separate current evidence.
